title: Check Day
takeaway: Twice a week, check your approvals on revoke.cash and revoke the ones you do not use, because disconnecting a site does not cancel them.

cards.title: You pressed Disconnect
cards.body: Last month you tried a free claim site, then pressed Disconnect in your wallet. You feel safe. But the permission you gave that site is still live. Disconnecting only hides your address from the site. This list shows what is really still allowed.

value.label: Marketplace you use
value.why: You list here weekly, so keep it.

value.label: Unlimited approval to unknown contract
value.why: You never knowingly approved this. Revoke it.

value.label: Old site you no longer use
value.why: You stopped using it. Revoke it.

cards.title: Approvals stay until you revoke them
cards.body: An approval is a permission you signed that lets a contract move your tokens or NFTs. It stays active until you revoke it. Pressing Disconnect does not cancel it. Marketplaces need approvals to work, so having some is normal. Unknown or old ones are the risk.
points: Disconnect only hides your address from the site.

cards.title: Check by address, no wallet needed
cards.body: Open revoke.cash from your own bookmark and paste your public address into the search box. Looking is read only, so you do not link your wallet to see the list. Etherscan's token approval checker shows Ethereum approvals too. Never open a checker from a DM, a reply or a search ad.
points: Never type your seed phrase on any checker.

cards.title: Revoke only what you do not know or use
cards.body: Each revoke is a small transaction, so on Ethereum each one costs gas. Revoke only what you do not recognise or no longer use. To revoke, you link your wallet on the real site you opened yourself, and confirm one revoke at a time.
points: Old site you stopped using: revoke.
Marketplace you use every week: keep.

cards.body: It is Check Day. Tap each approval you should revoke, then Done.

questions.stem: You pressed Disconnect on a shady site last week. Are the approvals you gave it cancelled?
options: No, they stay active until you revoke them
Yes, pressing Disconnect cancels every approval it had
Yes, after seven days they expire
Only if you close the browser too
questions.why: Disconnecting only stops the site seeing your address. Approvals stay active until you revoke them.

questions.stem: It is Check Day. What do you need to see your approvals on revoke.cash?
options: Only your public address in the search box
Your seed phrase to unlock the list
A signature from your vault to log in
A login code from a support DM
questions.why: The search is read only. Your public address is enough, and no wallet needs to be linked just to look.

questions.stem: Your list shows an approval to the marketplace where you list dragons every week. What do you do?
options: Keep it, because you still use it
Revoke it every Monday and Thursday
Revoke it and approve again daily
Revoke it, every approval is a risk
questions.why: Revoke only unknown or unused approvals. A marketplace you use needs its approval, and every revoke costs gas.

questions.stem: You find an unlimited USDC approval to a contract you do not recognise. What do you do?
options: Revoke it on revoke.cash from your bookmark
Leave it, since nothing has gone yet
Ask in a DM what it is
Disconnect the site to cancel it
questions.why: An unknown unlimited approval can let a contract take all that token. Revoke it on the real site.

questions.stem: A friend plans to revoke all 30 approvals every Check Day to be safe. What do you tell them?
options: Revoke only unknown or unused ones, each costs gas
Great plan, revoking everything is always the safest
Revoking is free, so do it even more often
Disconnect every site instead, it does the same
questions.why: Check Day means checking. Each revoke on Ethereum costs gas, so revoke only approvals you do not recognise or no longer use.

questions.why: A stranger DMed you first, pushed a lookalike revoke site and added a deadline. Open revoke.cash only from your own bookmark.

value.label: Unlimited approval to a site you left
value.why: You no longer use it. Revoke it.

value.label: Marketplace you use
value.why: You still list here. Keep it.

value.label: Unknown contract with all NFTs
value.why: You do not recognise it. Revoke it.

questions.why: The red flags are approvals to revoke: the unknown contract and the site you left. Keep the marketplace you still use, since every revoke costs gas.

questions.stem: You search for revoke cash and the top result is an ad. What do you do?
options: Skip it and open revoke.cash from your bookmark
Click it, search ads are checked first
Click it but only connect a vault
Use the first result that is not an ad
questions.why: Scammers buy search ads for fake revoke sites. Bookmark the real site once and always open it from there.

questions.stem: Besides revoke.cash, which tool also shows your Ethereum token approvals?
options: Etherscan's token approval checker, opened from a bookmark
Your wallet's list of sites you disconnected
A checker link a support bot sends
Any site that asks to link your wallet
questions.why: Etherscan's token approval checker also lists approvals. Your wallet's list of linked sites is not the same thing.
